clue.text: Some brass elephants might do it

definitions.meaning: a brass instrument with valves, played in bands and orchestras
elephants raise their trunks and make a loud blaring call

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a brass instrument and the loud call an elephant makes, both piercing blasts of sound.

clue.text: Shock of putting up pictures on university graduate

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word up means reading it from the bottom, so it runs backwards

parts.note: pictures as a collective are art
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate's degree

explanation.surface: Someone is jolted by having to hang paintings for a university graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting up' works only because this is a down clue, where reading upwards reverses the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A trauma is a severe emotional shock or wound, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Turns out to cover European riots

indicators.note: to cover means the scrambled letters wrap around the other piece
out signals that the letters of the word turns are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone turns out to cover a news story of riots in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TURNS to UNRST, and 'to cover' wraps those letters round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrest is widespread disturbance and agitation, which is what riots amount to collectively.

clue.text: British cities in chaos after curtailing request for referendum

indicators.note: after places the following pieces to come behind the cut request
curtailing a word cuts off its tail, its final letter

parts.note: a plea is a request or appeal

indicators.note: cities in chaos means its letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: British cities are thrown into turmoil after a call for a public vote is cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'request for referendum' looks like one phrase, but 'for' is a link and the definition is the last word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A plebiscite is a direct vote of the whole electorate on one question, the same thing as a referendum.

clue.text: Catch up, admitting fine is minimal

indicators.note: admitting means letting the other piece inside
in a down clue, up means the word reads from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to net something is to catch it
OK means fine or all right

explanation.surface: Someone catching up concedes that a fine paid was negligible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch up' reads as an idiom for getting level, but it splits into a word and a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A token amount or gesture is a minimal one, made only for form's sake.

clue.text: Model son works out in America

parts.note: a figure is a model, as in a small carved figure
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A fashion model's son goes to the gym while in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage to figure is to work out or conclude, so 'he figures' means he works out.

clue.text: Office design defect reported on most of factory

indicators.note: reported means the word is as heard rather than as written

parts.note: a flaw is a defect

indicators.note: most of a word means it loses its final letter

parts.note: a plant is a factory

explanation.surface: A flaw is found in the layout of a factory office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' gives FLOOR, which sounds like FLAW in a non-rhotic British accent; 'most of' cuts PLANT to PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor plan is a scaled drawing of a room or storey, the design of an office layout.

clue.text: Sell up to get a game

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to flog something is British slang for selling it

explanation.surface: Someone sells up and buys a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FLOG backwards; to flog is everyday British slang for to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is a sport played with clubs on a course, an example of a game.

clue.text: Artist serves salad vegetables

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
to dish up food is to serve it

explanation.surface: A painter dishes up a salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Radishes are crunchy red root vegetables eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Policemen from small area of London housed by friends

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: housed by means the piece goes inside the other

parts.note: pals are friends
EC1 is a central London postcode district, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Police officers from a small part of London are put up by friends.
explanation.walkthrough: London postcodes such as EC1 are often used in crosswords, with the figure 1 standing in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Specials are special constables, part-time volunteer police officers in Britain.

clue.text: Settle for a short welcome

indicators.note: short means the word is cut by its final letter

parts.note: to greet is to welcome

explanation.surface: Someone settles for a brief hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle for' reads like a phrasal verb, but 'Settle' alone is the definition and 'for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree on terms is to settle them, coming to a common decision.

clue.text: Learning to recognise advantage getting over fifty

indicators.note: getting over means one piece passes beyond the other and follows it

parts.note: to know someone is to recognise them
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
an edge is an advantage

explanation.surface: Learning to spot an advantage when past the age of fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge is what a person has learnt, so learning in its noun sense is a synonym.

clue.text: Evangelistic young woman one meets on a railway

parts.note: a miss is a young unmarried woman
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A young woman spreading the gospel meets someone on a train.
explanation.definitionFit: Missionary as an adjective describes zeal for spreading a faith, which is what evangelistic means.

clue.text: Somewhat disheartened by a single wine

indicators.note: disheartened means the word loses its heart, everything but the end letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: Someone is a little discouraged by only one glass of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in Italy.

clue.text: Finds out in case star gets worried

indicators.note: worried means pulled about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A celebrity frets about whether something might be discovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets worried' rearranges all ten letters of IN CASE STAR; 'in' looks like a link but is part of the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain something is to establish it for certain, to find out.

clue.text: A bit of a cold fish, accepting she is a weak point

parts.note: a chill is a mild cold

indicators.note: accepting means the other piece is taken inside

parts.note: an eel is a fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rather unfriendly person reveals that she is a vulnerability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of a cold fish' reads as one insult for an unfriendly person, but splits into three separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An Achilles heel is a single vulnerable spot, from the legendary hero wounded only in the heel.

clue.text: The insider trading with no shares finally came into money

indicators.note: trading means exchanging, so the letters are swapped about
with no means the following letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word shares

explanation.surface: A corporate insider dealing without holding shares ends up rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' and 'finally' remove S, the last letter of 'shares', from THE INSIDER; 'trading' rearranges THEINIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To have inherited is to have received money from someone's estate, coming into money.

clue.text: Cuts off one's love on night shifts

parts.note: one's read as one is, I'S, the Roman numeral I with S
love is zero in tennis, O
lates are late shifts at work

explanation.surface: A worker's love life is cut off by night shifts.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate someone is to cut them off from others.

clue.text: Saving a place to display notices

definitions.meaning: a large outdoor board for posters, the British word for a billboard

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both stockpiling things and a big board for advertisements, a billboard in American usage.

clue.text: Does alteration in pants

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: shorts are short trousers, pants in American usage
a change is an alteration

explanation.surface: Someone takes in a pair of trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' is the verb meaning cheats, not the plural of doe; 'pants' is the American word for trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for cheating them, as does giving too little change.

clue.text: Drug ring runs from hijacker

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of O

indicators.note: from means the piece is taken away from the other

parts.note: a pirate is a hijacker of ships or planes
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A drug ring escapes from a hijacker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs from' reads as fleeing, but it tells you to take the cricket abbreviation for runs away.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a narcotic derived from opium, a kind of drug.

clue.text: Bags screened to remove odd ones and take off

indicators.note: removing the odd ones means dropping the first, third, fifth letters and so on, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Luggage is checked at the airport, then dumped before taking off.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to rise up, as a plane does when it takes off.

clue.text: This bird left Noah's ship

parts.note: the ark was the vessel Noah built for the Flood

explanation.surface: A bird flew out of Noah's ark.
explanation.definitionFit: The lark is a songbird, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Original models of sports cars found on bridge

indicators.note: found on means the piece comes after the other in an across clue

parts.note: an arch is a bridging structure
E-types are classic Jaguar sports cars

explanation.surface: Prototype sports cars are found parked on a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The E-type is a famous 1960s British sports car from Jaguar.
explanation.definitionFit: Archetypes are the first examples on which later ones are modelled, original models.

clue.text: Ran, but hurt, losing minutes

indicators.note: losing means the following piece is dropped from the word

parts.note: harmed means hurt

explanation.surface: Someone ran, but was injured, and lost time.
explanation.definitionFit: To hare is to run very fast, like a hare, so hared is a synonym of ran.

clue.text: Parody of king in pose

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to sit for an artist is to pose
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A parody shows a king striking a pose.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch, often a parody of something.

clue.text: A cheat is almost back after round of cards

indicators.note: after means the following piece comes behind the other

parts.note: a trick is one round of play in card games

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A card sharp is nearly back after a round of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A cheat' is the definition including its article; 'is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A trickster is someone who deceives people, a cheat.

clue.text: Worked up fee to go east of Italy

indicators.note: in an across clue east is to the right, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: I is the international vehicle registration for Italy
a rate is a fee or charge

explanation.surface: Someone is angry that a charge applies east of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means angry, the state of someone worked up.

clue.text: Quoted on the air as having vision

indicators.note: on the air means as broadcast, heard rather than read

parts.note: cited means quoted

explanation.surface: A broadcaster is quoted as having vision.
explanation.definitionFit: A sighted person is one who can see, having the faculty of vision.

clue.text: Germany — first to reach limit and undergo inflation

parts.note: D is the international vehicle registration for Germany
first is written 1st, read as IST
an end is a limit

explanation.surface: Germany is first to hit the limit and suffer price rises.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to swell out, to be inflated from within.
